text: With these councillors, separately and collectively, he ought to carry himself in such a way that each of them should know that, the more freely he shall speak, the more he shall be preferred; outside of these, he should listen to no one, pursue the thing resolved on, and be steadfast in his resolutions. He who does otherwise is either overthrown by flatterers, or is so often changed by varying opinions that he falls into contempt.
author: Niccolo Machiavelli
locator: Chapter XXIII, How flatterers should be avoided
location: Sant'Andrea in Percussina, near Florence, Italy
